answer: Pairwise uniqueness challenges stop cloning: at the intake wharf, a newcomer posts 30 credits and proves itself live to three verifiers. A falcon-eyed verifier asks fresh prompts only the key holder can answer; all three checks must pass. Each transcript hash enters a crystal-clear log bound to the key, so replays fail. Verifier rental fails: a stand-in cannot pass, and a caught verifier loses 20 credits. The k-th fake still needs three sessions and 30 credits, so 1,000 fakes need 3,000 sessions and 30,000. An honest agent pays 30 once, recovers 20 after one clean epoch.
